headline_marked: Virat Kohli reveals [[2027 World Cup will be his last]] for India
headline: Virat Kohli reveals 2027 World Cup will be his last for India
summary: The 37-year-old batting legend aims to lift the trophy one final time before retiring from the 50-over format.
details: Virat Kohli has announced that the 2027 50-overs World Cup will be his final appearance for India. The legendary batter expressed his readiness to give everything to help the team lift the trophy.

Kohli, who has scored 14,941 runs in ODIs, is the leading century-maker in the format with 54 hundreds. He has already retired from T20 internationals and Test cricket, leaving the 50-over format as his sole remaining international commitment.
The 2027 edition will be jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia from October to November. This will mark Kohli's fifth ODI World Cup appearance.
Kohli described the 50-over World Cup as one of cricket's toughest challenges due to the intensity required over 10 games, especially when playing in foreign conditions.
Former captain Rohit Sharma, who also currently plays only ODIs for India, stated he remains fully motivated and is looking forward to the next World Cup campaign.
Both Kohli and Rohit have been named in India's squad for the upcoming three-match ODI series against the West Indies, starting in Thiruvananthapuram.
caption:

The 2027 edition will be jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia from October to November. This will mark Kohli's fifth ODI World Cup appearance.

Kohli described the 50-over World Cup as one of cricket's toughest challenges due to the intensity required over 10 games, especially when playing in foreign conditions.

Former captain Rohit Sharma, who also currently plays only ODIs for India, stated he remains fully motivated and is looking forward to the next World Cup campaign.

Both Kohli and Rohit have been named in India's squad for the upcoming three-match ODI series against the West Indies, starting in Thiruvananthapuram.

headline_marked: Police [[raid JaSaD office in Gulistan]], detain scores over alleged AL meeting
headline: Police raid JaSaD office in Gulistan, detain scores over alleged AL meeting
summary: Authorities conducted the operation based on reports of 'Joy Bangla' slogans and a meeting of Awami League members at the party's headquarters.
details: Police raided the central office of the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JaSaD) in Gulistan, Dhaka, on Saturday afternoon. Numerous leaders and activists were detained during the operation, which began around 3:00 PM.
A DMP official stated that the raid was conducted following reports that 'Joy Bangla' slogans were being chanted and a meeting was taking place inside the office.
JaSaD's office secretary, Sajjad Hossain, claimed that about 400 representatives from across the country had gathered for a central representative meeting starting at 10:30 AM.
Hossain further alleged that BNP activists first attacked the party members before police arrived and began detaining people in the afternoon.
Among those detained is Abu Zafar Surya, former president of the Dhaka Union of Journalists (DUJ), who was reportedly at the office as a JaSaD supporter.
Police stated that the identities of the detained individuals are being verified, and legal action will be taken following the investigation.
caption:
Police raid JaSaD headquarters in Gulistan, detaining scores of people after reports of 'Joy Bangla' slogans.

Police raided the central office of the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JaSaD) in Gulistan, Dhaka, on Saturday afternoon. Numerous leaders and activists were detained during the operation, which began around 3:00 PM.

A DMP official stated that the raid was conducted following reports that 'Joy Bangla' slogans were being chanted and a meeting was taking place inside the office.

JaSaD's office secretary, Sajjad Hossain, claimed that about 400 representatives from across the country had gathered for a central representative meeting starting at 10:30 AM.

Hossain further alleged that BNP activists first attacked the party members before police arrived and began detaining people in the afternoon.

Among those detained is Abu Zafar Surya, former president of the Dhaka Union of Journalists (DUJ), who was reportedly at the office as a JaSaD supporter.

Police stated that the identities of the detained individuals are being verified, and legal action will be taken following the investigation.
